message.text:
h08.

There are exactly two declarers, both named `Runner` but in different packages. Only the S3 presign one is actually invoked; the memo-payload runner's `RunOnce` is dead code — its package is imported only for the standalone `RebuildMemoPayload` function.

**Answer:**

```
*s3presign.Runner (server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:43) — yes — server/server.go:163 (startBackgroundRunners), and internally at server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:36 (Run's ticker loop)
*memopayload.Runner (server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:27) — no — no caller in the repository (no test caller either)
```

Evidence:

- A repo-wide search for `RunOnce` in Go files returns only five hits: the two method declarations above, plus three references, all of which belong to the `s3presign` type — `server/server.go:163`, `server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:36`, and the declaration itself. No interface anywhere declares a `RunOnce` method, so there is no indirect dispatch to consider.

- The invoked declaration is reached two ways, both in production code. It runs once synchronously at startup and then on every tick:

```161:163:server/server.go
	// Create and start S3 presign runner
	s3presignRunner := s3presign.NewRunner(s.Store)
	s3presignRunner.RunOnce(ctx)
```

```33:40:server/runner/s3presign/runner.go
	for {
		select {
		case <-ticker.C:
			r.RunOnce(ctx)
		case <-ctx.Done():
			return
		}
	}
```

- `memopayload.Runner` is entirely unconstructed: `memopayload.NewRunner` (`server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:19`) has zero call sites — the only `NewRunner(` invocation in the repo is `s3presign.NewRunner` at `server/server.go:162`. The single importer of the package, `server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:18`, uses only the package-level `RebuildMemoPayload` helper, at `server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:108` and `:447` (which `RunOnce` also calls internally, at `server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:52`). So the type, its constructor, and its `RunOnce` bulk-rebuild loop are unreachable, while the underlying per-memo logic is very much live.
